description.narrative: Protection of Human and Democratic Rights, Promotion of Rule of Law & Good Governance and Peace Building

Protection of Human and Democratic Rights, Promotion of Rule of Law & Good Governance and Peace Building. Justice For All - Prison fellowship Ethiopia (JFA-PFE) is an NGO which started its activities in 1992, supporting prisoners in Ethiopia. The organisation has gradually widened its operations to include human rights, rule of law and capacity building and advocacy in the justice sector justice. Recently JFA-PFE also engaged in reconciliation and peace-building. Sweden has supported JFA-PFE since the mid 2000s. The current program, "Justice 2022-2025, An Integrated Program on Protection of Human Rights, Strengthening of Rule of Law and Peace Building Process in Ethiopia" is supported by Sweden, Norway, Netherlands and Austria. This program was developed from JFA's new strategic plan "Creating the Future" 2021-2025 that was completed and approved in July 2021.JFA submitted the proposal in March 2022 and after reviewing the document, extensive comments were given to the cooperation partner to re-work on the proposal as well as to present a more realistic budget. The revised proposal was submitted in July 2022. The donors, have since been engaging with the cooperation partner to clarify and respond to certain questions that arose during the appraisal process.The budget for 3,5 years (2022-2025) is approx. 7,7 MUSD: The Swedish contribution is set to 20 MSEK, with 5MSEK/year. Other donors have pledged the following: The Netherlands 400000EUR/year, Austria 500000Euro/year (starting in 2023) and Norway NOK 5M/year.

The overall goal of the project is:
"Contribution to enhanced status of rights, rule of law, peace building process and improved justice system in Ethiopia through advocacy, quiet lobby and capacity building trainings for the three branches of the government"
The following three strategic objectives and results shall be realized to fulfil the overall goal of the project:
Strategic Objective 1: Strengthen Rule of Law in Ethiopia through improved institutional capacity of the justice sector to enact laws, policies, and create better access to Justice and improved Leadership capacity of justice sector.
Strategic Objective 2: Strengthen promotion of Human Rights in Ethiopia through enhanced capacity of the legislative, executive & judiciary and media to respect and protect fulfilment of rights.
Strategic Objective 3: Support peace building in Ethiopia through enhanced capacity of stakeholders in peace building process, Traditional Peace Building Practices and Inclusive dialogue in Ethiopia.

description.narrative:
Support to legal and policy reforms: JFA supported the development, revision, and validation of key legal and policy instruments, including four draft bills, four revised proclamations, and one policy document. These reforms covered alternatives to imprisonment, reintegration, legal aid, disaster risk management, and improvements to federal judicial administration and court procedures.
Development of the first EnglishAfaan Oromo legal dictionary: JFA supported the development of a standardized legal dictionary to improve consistency in legal terminology, strengthen legal communication, and enhance access to justice.
Development of a standardized orthography manual: A standardized orthography manual was developed to promote consistency in legal terminology and public administration.
Support for court backlog clearance: JFA supported backlog reduction efforts in federal and regional courts, resulting in the disposal of 17,500 cases. As a direct result, 1,132 detainees and prisoners were released, while more than 1,415 cases involving women and children were resolved, contributing to improved access to justice and protection of vulnerable groups.
Support for prosecution backlog clearance: Through support to the Ministry of Justice, JFA contributed to the review and clearance of 1,000 backlogged prosecution files, with an additional 436 cases determined unsuitable for further prosecution.
Facilitation of pardon and forgiveness processes: JFA supported pardon and forgiveness processes that contributed to the release of 3,455 inmates, including 184 women, helping reduce prison overcrowding and prioritizing vulnerable groups, including elderly prisoners, persons with serious illnesses, women with children, and juveniles.
Establishment of a child-friendly court bench in Hawassa: JFA supported the establishment of a child-friendly bench at Hawassa First Instance Court in the Sidama Region to provide a safer and more child-sensitive justice process for child victims and witnesses.
Public Legal Education Campaign: JFA partnered with Fana Media Corporation to produce a 14-part human rights media series broadcast through 28 weekly programs covering issues such as alternative sentencing, sexual and gender-based violence, digital justice, hate speech, and civil rights. The campaign reached more than 249,998 people through mainstream media.
Advocating and Scaling Up Alternatives to Imprisonment: JFA supported the expansion and institutionalization of alternative sentencing mechanisms in South Ethiopia and Central Ethiopia and contributed to the development of a national draft proclamation on alternatives to imprisonment. The initiative progressed toward national adoption, and some courts, including the Konso Zone High Court, replicated the approach within their own institutions. Advanced Prison Reform through the Validation of Key Legal Frameworks: JFA supported the review and validation of draft legal reforms on prisoner reintegration, correctional standards, and alternatives to imprisonment prior to their submission for legislative approval.
Established income generating initiative for women prisoners: To strengthen the rehabilitation and economic reintegration of women prisoners, JFA procured and installed a bread-baking machine and related equipment at Kality Prison. The facility has a production capacity of 400 loaves per hour. The partner also provided entrepreneurship, bookkeeping, and business planning training to 48 women inmates (conducted during the NCE period in 2026), equipping them with practical skills that can support their rehabilitation and future livelihoods.
Human Rights and Prison Assessments: Two studies were conducted, one on human rights conditions and rehabilitation gaps in Ethiopian prisons and another on the military justice system, producing evidence and recommendations to inform future reforms.
Elder-led Mediation held to deescalate tension between Tigray and Federal Actors: In collaboration with the Ethiopian Elders' Council, Peace Mothers, and prominent business leaders, JFA-PFE facilitated a series of consultations on dialogue and peaceful conflict resolution. The Elders' Council conducted consultations with government officials and other stakeholders from both the Federal Government and Tigray, while JFA-PFE provided financial, logistical, and technical support, including expert input to the development of the Council's code of conduct for peace mediation. As a result of these consultations and follow-up engagements, a joint task force was established between representatives of the Federal Government and the TPLF to address outstanding areas of disagreement and advance reconciliation efforts.
Restorative Justice (RJ) Expanded: During the reporting period, customary courts were formally launched in the Amhara Region, institutionalizing restorative justice mechanisms. Also in Southwest Ethiopia Region, 399 kebeles are now practicing restorative justice. The initiative has reduced the burden on formal courts in the region.
Strategic Partnership established to advance National Dialogue: A partnership was established between the Ethiopian National Dialogue Commission (ENDC) and the Ethiopian Elders' Council (EEC). The partnership is intended to support agenda setting, participation, and future national dialogue processes.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
